testCases.description: A backward clock jump neither drains existing tokens nor lowers the per-key refill watermark.

clarifyingQuestions: Are limits per user, org, endpoint, model, or a tuple of dimensions?
Can a single request cost more than one token?
Should retry_after be rounded up for HTTP callers?
followUps: Add separate request-token, input-token, and output-token buckets.
Add priority tiers with different capacities and refill rates.
Make `allow` thread-safe with one lock around refill and consume.
followUpGuide: For multiple dimensions, refill and inspect every required bucket before consuming any. Commit every debit only if all dimensions allow; calling allow on each bucket sequentially can spend tokens on an ultimately denied request. If any blocks, return the maximum deficit delay across blockers. Protect the combined decision atomically under concurrency.

For priority tiers, resolve the tier before lookup and decide whether tiers share one caller balance or have separate caller/tier buckets. If policy changes for an existing bucket, explicitly migrate its capacity/rate and refill timestamp; do not grant an accidental fresh burst by changing keys.
For thread safety, guard the read-refill-consume write sequence with one `threading.Lock`; splitting that sequence allows two callers to spend the same tokens.
complexityAnalysis: - Token bucket (this problem): refill from elapsed time and update one balance per key. Time: O(1) average per allow using a hash map. Space: O(K) total for K remembered keys; idle keys are not evicted automatically.

- Related pattern (rolling window of timestamps): store accepted requests and prune by their ages. Time: O(k) per call for a naive scan of k retained requests. Space: O(k) per key. Rolling windows measure quota over time; token buckets model burst capacity with continuous refill.
solutionGuide: Track `(tokens, last_seen)` per key, clamping `effective_now = max(now, last_seen)` so backward clock jumps neither subtract existing tokens nor overwrite the monotonic refill watermark. On every call, refill by `(effective_now - last_seen) * refill_rate_per_second`, capped at `capacity`.
If `tokens >= cost`, subtract `cost` and allow. Otherwise store `(tokens, effective_now)` and compute `(cost - tokens) / refill_rate_per_second` as `retry_after`.
